Plot unipolar survey responses as a serpentine of single-hue stacked bars

Source: R/survey_sequence.R
sequential_dist.Rd

Some rating scales have no neutral midpoint: frequency scales from "Never" to "Always", or intensity scales from "Not at all" to "Extremely". For such scales a diverging palette suggests a midpoint the scale does not have. sequential_dist() draws the display of survey_sequence(), one 100% stacked bar per item along a serpentine, with a light-to-dark palette of a single hue, so that darker segments stand for higher levels.

Input, sorting, labels and layout options are those of survey_sequence(); hue sets the color of the palette. For bipolar (agree-disagree) scales use survey_sequence(); to show individual responses use survey_snake().

Usage

sequential_dist(
  counts,
  labels = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  hue = 210,
  band_height = 28,
  band_gap = 14,
  plot_width = 500,
  colors = NULL,
  show_percent = TRUE,
  min_segment = 34,
  arc_style = c("gradient", "neutral"),
  arc_opacity = 0.85,
  sort_by = c("none", "mean", "net"),
  shadow = TRUE,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  label_color = "#333333",
  label_size = 0.85,
  label_align = "left",
  reverse_rtl = FALSE,
  start_from = c("left", "right"),
  flow = c("snake", "natural"),
  title = NULL,
  margin = c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 55, left = 100),
  background = "white"
)

Arguments

counts

Responses: a data frame of raw responses (one row per respondent, one column per item), a numeric matrix of counts (items in rows, response levels in columns), or a data frame of counts. A data frame is read as raw responses when its columns hold few distinct whole-number or categorical values relative to its number of rows.

labels

Item labels, one per item. NULL (default) uses the row names of a count table, or, for raw responses, the column names with the number of responses.

levels

Response levels in scale order. NULL (default) uses the column names of a count table, or, for raw responses, the factor levels or the sorted distinct values. For raw responses the levels must match the values in the data.

hue

Hue of the palette in degrees, 0-360 (default 210, blue).

band_height

Height of each band in plot units (default 28).

band_gap

Gap between bands in plot units (default 14).

plot_width

Length of each band in plot units (default 500).

colors

One color per response level, in scale order. NULL (default) uses a light-to-dark palette of hue.

show_percent

Print percentages inside the segments (default TRUE).

min_segment

Minimum segment width, in plot units, for a percentage to be printed (default 34).

arc_style

"gradient" (default) colors each U-turn midway between the levels at its two ends; "neutral" draws it grey.

arc_opacity

Opacity of the U-turns, between 0 and 1 (default 0.85).

sort_by

Order of the items: "none" (default, input order), "mean" (increasing item mean) or "net" (increasing share of responses above the middle level minus share below; the mean for scales with fewer than four levels).

shadow

Draw drop shadows (default TRUE).

show_legend

Draw the legend (default TRUE).

label_color, label_size

Color and size multiplier of the item labels (defaults "#333333" and 0.85).

label_align

Alignment of the item labels: "left" (default), "right", or "direction" to follow each band's reading direction.

reverse_rtl

Reverse the order of levels on bands that read right to left, so every band starts with the lowest level in its reading direction (default FALSE: lowest level on the left of every band).

start_from

Side on which the first band starts: "left" (default) or "right".

flow

"snake" (default): bands alternate direction. "natural": every band reads in the same direction.

title

Plot title, or NULL (default) for none.

margin

Named numeric vector of top, right, bottom and left margins in plot units (default c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 55, left = 100)).

background

Background color (default "white").

Value

The value of survey_sequence(): the plot is drawn on the current device and an object of class snake_layout is returned invisibly.

References

Heiberger, R. M., & Robbins, N. B. (2014). Design of diverging stacked bar charts for Likert scales and other applications. Journal of Statistical Software, 57(5), 1-32. doi:10.18637/jss.v057.i05

See also

survey_sequence() for diverging colors; survey_snake() for individual responses; snake_palette() for the sequential palettes "blues", "greens", "grays", "warm" and "viridis".

Examples

# Emotion intensity rated 1-5, a unipolar scale
sequential_dist(ema_emotions, sort_by = "mean", hue = 160)


# A table of counts on a frequency scale
counts <- matrix(c(15, 25, 60, 80, 45,
                   10, 20, 50, 90, 55,
                   20, 30, 65, 70, 40),
                 nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
sequential_dist(counts,
                labels = c("Plans study time", "Reviews notes",
                           "Asks for help"),
                levels = c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Often",
                           "Always"))
